calls.reason: The October 2025 EBU/BBC study found significant issues in 45% of answers across four leading assistants. Fortune's Deloitte report documents consequential fabrications, supporting persistent reliability problems despite improvements.

CEPA found few EU imitators in April, while Vietnam later adopted a similar framework. This mixed evidence does not establish whether much of the world increasingly sought European guidance, which need not mean copying its laws.

Engadget confirms Alexa's upgrade missed 2024, but GSMArena documents Gemini Live's release that year. Without assessments of its improvement over existing assistants, Alexa alone cannot settle the broader claim.

CNBC and Fortune describe major model makers' losses and financial struggles. Reports on Inflection, Adept and, less securely, Covariant indicate modest or negligible investor gains; Character.AI's larger return does not negate those three.

Census data show limited but rising AI use, without measuring prior expectations. Fortune's projected OpenAI loss supports financial difficulties but cannot establish aggregate industry profits or the combined claim.

ATA documents millions of human drivers, but Baidu reports substantial Chinese driverless operations and Waymo describes adverse-weather capabilities. The packet lacks comparable geographic and weather usage data to call the whole claim.
